correctness.rationale: For each n>=2 and -1<t<=1/n, the claimed cap-containing ellipsoid is positive definite and its squared radial surplus is precisely 2(1-nt)(1-z)(z+t)/((n-1)(1+t)), nonnegative for the whole cap. Its affine normalization maps one apex and a regular base simplex to an inscribed regular n-simplex, attaining the affine-scaled full-ball maximum. The covariance determinant proof includes the equality characterization for any contained simplex. Strict surplus forces apex/base contacts below the transition; at t=1/n the regular-simplex vertical coordinate moment identity forces precisely one apex. For larger caps the full-ball optimum is feasible and all maximizers must be inscribed regular n-simplices. Rational arithmetic checks independently validate the critical identities, and finite Monte Carlo checks supplement but do not prove the theorem.

value.rationale: The question concerns a canonical n-dimensional convex body of practical extremal geometric interest and was explicitly posed with no known upper bound sharpness in the 2015 source. Proving a sharp whole-family invariant, the exact saturation height 1+1/n, and all geometric equality cases supplies meaningful structure, not only an arbitrary numerical slice or an already-tabulated construction.
